meaning: Relative importance of a typical within-view difference in each score component. fit.py converts importance to a prior weight by dividing by the mean absolute within-pair difference of that component across all pairs (layout data only, no ratings). Only the relative shape is a prior; overall scale is free.

basis.congestion: Literature. Edge crossings had the largest effect on graph comprehension in Purchase (1997) and Purchase, Carrington and Allder (2002), and on path-tracing in Ware, Purchase, Colpoys and McGill (2002). Congestion here combines crossing points with shared lane length.
basis.bends: Literature. Bends ranked second after crossings in Purchase (1997); path continuity mattered in Ware et al. (2002).
basis.occlusion: Judgment, informed by 3D graph studies such as Ware and Franck (1996): hidden objects and paths cannot be read. No 2D study measures this term directly.
basis.route_length: Literature, weaker. Ware et al. (2002) found total path length affects path tracing, but less than crossings or continuity.
basis.compactness: Judgment. Area and overall compactness show weak or inconsistent effects in 2D studies; kept moderate for an overview-first 3D view.
basis.aspect_ratio: Judgment. No strong empirical support; kept low.
basis.distortion: Judgment. Size distortion from preferred dimensions is a presentation-fidelity term; kept low.
